internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root shows up only as a Form II verb, three times, in just two verse-settings. In 39:5 God 'winds' the night over the day and the day over the night — the very same act done both ways, which tells us kwr is about wrapping/overlaying one thing over another, and the verse itself keeps it distinct from creating, harnessing, and making-run. In 81:1 'when the sun is kuwwirat', the sun is acted on alone, passively, at the end of the world; here the text gives us only 'something terminal happens to the sun' — the specific 'wound-up/rolled-up' reading is a plausible extension of 39:5 but is not proven from the Quranic wording, so that token is held as an unresolved seam rather than forced into the nucleus.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: kwr does NOT mean: (1) create/originate — خَلَقَ is used separately in 39:5 for the heavens and earth; (2) harness/subdue — سَخَّرَ is the verb for sun/moon in the same verse; (3) cause-to-run/course — يَجْرِى لِأَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى is the coursing verb, contrasted in-verse; (4) one-directional covering/veiling/darkening — because the day is wound over the night as well (39:5:9:2), the act must be symmetric, so 'cast darkness over' is excluded; (5) insertion/threading — the frame is عَلَى ('over'), never فِي ('into'); (6) intrinsic destruction/shattering — nothing is unmade in 39:5, so any 'collapse/extinguish' sense at 81:1 is contextual (Sūra 81 dissolution catalogue), not lexical. internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: The best competitor to the winding nucleus is 'cover over / cause to go dark'. It fits 81:1 (sun goes dark) and half of 39:5 (night covers day).
